content.page_summary: Reference list focusing on exercise training, rehabilitation, and clinic-based management in heart failure (particularly heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, HFpEF). Includes randomized trials, systematic reviews/meta-analyses, Cochrane review, and registry/epidemiologic studies addressing exercise interventions, endothelial function, quality of life, clinic follow-up, and use of evidence-based therapy.

332.citation: Edelmann F, Gelbrich G, Dungen HD, Frohling S, Wachter R, Stahrenberg R, Binder L, Topper A, Lashki DJ, Schwarz S, Herrmann-Lingen C, Loffler M, Hasenfuss G, Halle M, Pieske B.
332.title: Exercise training improves exercise capacity and diastolic function in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: results of the Ex-DHF (Exercise training in Diastolic Heart Failure) pilot study.
332.notes: Pilot randomized/exercise training study in HFpEF demonstrating improvements in exercise capacity and diastolic function.

333.citation: Nolte K, Herrmann-Lingen C, Wachter R, Gelbrich G, Dungen HD, Duvinage A, Hoischen N, von Oehsen K, Schwarz S, Hasenfuss G, Halle M, Pieske B, Edelmann F.
333.title: Effects of exercise training on different quality of life dimensions in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: the Ex-DHF-P trial.
333.notes: Examines quality-of-life outcomes after exercise training in HFpEF (Ex-DHF-P trial).

334.citation: Ismail H, McFarlane JR, Nojoumian AH, Dieberg G, Smart NA.
334.title: Clinical outcomes and cardiovascular responses to different exercise training intensities in patients with heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
334.notes: Systematic review/meta-analysis comparing exercise intensities and cardiovascular/clinical outcomes in heart failure patients.

335.citation: Kitzman DW, Brubaker PH, Herrington DM, Morgan TM, Stewart KP, Hundley WG, Abdelhamed A, Haykowsky MJ.
335.title: Effect of endurance exercise training on endothelial function and arterial stiffness in older patients with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction: a randomized, controlled, single-blind trial.
335.notes: Randomized trial assessing effects of endurance exercise on endothelial function and arterial stiffness in older HFpEF patients.

336.citation: Ismail H, McFarlane J, Smart NA.
336.title: Is exercise training beneficial for heart failure patients taking beta-adrenergic blockers? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
336.notes: Evaluates interaction between exercise training benefits and concurrent beta-blocker therapy in heart failure.

337.citation: Kitzman DW, Brubaker P, Morgan T, Haykowsky M, Hundley G, Kraus WE, Eggebeen J, Nicklas BJ.
337.title: Effect of caloric restriction or aerobic exercise training on peak oxygen consumption and quality of life in obese older patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: a randomized clinical trial.
337.notes: Randomized clinical trial comparing caloric restriction vs aerobic exercise in obese older HFpEF patients; outcomes included peak VO2 and quality of life.

338.citation: Taylor RS, Sagar VA, Davies EJ, Briscoe S, Coats AJ, Dalal H, Lough F, Rees K, Singh S.
338.title: Exercise-based rehabilitation for heart failure.
338.notes: Cochrane systematic review on exercise-based rehabilitation in heart failure.

339.citation: Schou M, Gustafsson F, Videbaek L, Tuxen C, Keller N, Handberg J, Sejr Knudsen A, Espersen G, Markenvard J, Egstrup K, Ulriksen H, Hildebrandt PR, the NorthStar Investigators, all members of The Danish Heart Failure Clinics Network.
339.title: Extended heart failure clinic follow-up in low-risk patients: a randomized clinical trial (NorthStar).
339.notes: Randomized trial of extended clinic follow-up for low-risk HF patients (NorthStar) assessing follow-up strategies.

340.citation: Thorvaldsen T, Benson L, Dahlstrom U, Edner M, Lund LH.
340.title: Use of evidence-based therapy and survival in heart failure in Sweden 2003-2012.
340.notes: Registry/epidemiologic study from Sweden relating use of evidence-based HF therapies to survival over 2003–2012.

341.citation: Lund LH, Braunschweig F, Benson L, Stahlberg M, Dahlstrom U, Linde C.
341.title: Association between demographic, organizational, clinical, and socio-economic characteristics and underutilization of cardiac resynchronization therapy: results from the Swedish Heart Failure Registry.
341.notes: Registry analysis identifying factors associated with underutilization of CRT in Swedish HF patients.

key_topics: Exercise training effects in heart failure and HFpEF (capacity, diastolic function, endothelial function, arterial stiffness)
Quality of life outcomes after exercise interventions
Intensity of exercise training and clinical outcomes
Interaction of exercise benefits with beta-blocker therapy
Caloric restriction vs aerobic exercise in obese HFpEF patients
Clinic follow-up models and registry-based evaluations of therapy use and outcomes
